raised.claim: The public registration route relies entirely on an external per-client limit that the rollout leaves unapplied at deployment.
raised.why_it_breaks: Without the edge rule, a single source can consume the shared daily allocation, leaving legitimate installations unable to register until Warsaw midnight. The cap bounds total registrations but does not reserve any capacity for other callers.

raised.claim: Registration validates the version only after parsing a body that can be as large as the app-wide limit.
raised.why_it_breaks: A JSON object with a valid version and a large unused property is buffered and parsed before validation strips the extra property. The global allowance accommodates multi-megabyte festival menus, so it does not protect this small public endpoint from disproportionate parsing and allocation work, even after the registration cap is reached.

raised.claim: Malformed registration JSON can be turned into a 500 by the app-wide error handler.
raised.why_it_breaks: For a request marked as JSON whose body is truncated, Hono's JSON validator throws a 400 HTTP exception before Zod validation; the shown app error handler ignores the exception status and responds with `500 internal`.

raised.claim: A capped registration still requires a successful synchronous write transaction before the route can return 429.
raised.why_it_breaks: If another SQLite connection holds the writer lock, the immediate transaction can block the shared event loop until the busy timeout, then return 500 instead of 429 if the lock is still held. This affects requests that cannot register regardless of whether the rejection counter can be written.

raised.claim: The cap alert uses a fixed 24-hour interval rather than the Warsaw date used by the registration cap.
raised.why_it_breaks: With an elapsed-time throttle, an alert late on Monday suppresses a fresh cap event early on Tuesday. Conversely, on Warsaw's 25-hour autumn clock-change day, two refusals 24 hours apart can both qualify while still falling on the same Warsaw date.

raised.claim: The best-effort journal, install counters, and version update are coupled so a failure in one skips unrelated writes.
raised.why_it_breaks: If a trigger rejects an insert into `match_misses`, a successful `/match` response still loses its install request and beer counts and its version update, even though both destination tables are writable. A failure in the usage insert similarly prevents the version update.

raised.quote:
const now = new Date();
    const date = warsawDateAndHour(now).date;
raised.claim: The aggregate and per-install ledgers can assign the same `/match` request to different Warsaw dates.
raised.why_it_breaks: A request counted in `api_usage` just before midnight can finish the awaited catalog and matching work after midnight, when the install ledger takes a fresh timestamp. The two daily request totals then disagree even though every write succeeded.

raised.claim: The resolver reports today's date as persisted even if the last-seen write failed.
raised.why_it_breaks: If the auth-time touch fails transiently and `/match` later supplies the same version already stored, `touchInstall` can skip the second write because the principal falsely says today's date was saved. The row retains yesterday's date despite a later opportunity to update it.

raised.claim: Bearer resolution updates install activity even when the endpoint subsequently rejects the caller.
raised.why_it_breaks: An install presenting its token only on a user-only endpoint receives 403 but advances `last_seen_date` anyway. That records a rejected request as install activity; an invalid `/match` body likewise refreshes the date before schema validation rejects it.

raised.quote:
db.prepare('UPDATE extension_installs SET last_seen_date = ?, ext_version = ? WHERE install_id = ?')
      .run(args.date, version, install.installId);
raised.claim: A date-only touch rewrites the version from a previously read snapshot.
raised.why_it_breaks: If two connections load the same install and one commits a new extension version before the other's date-only touch executes, the latter restores the stale version even though its caller supplied no version change.

raised.claim: `touchInstall` reports a write even when its UPDATE affects no row.
raised.why_it_breaks: If the install is deleted after its row is loaded, passing that snapshot to `touchInstall` returns `true` when a date or version differs, although there is no row left to update.

raised.quote: client: z.object({ version: z.string().max(64).optional(), shop: z.string().max(64).optional() }).optional(),
raised.claim: `/match` can overwrite the stored version with a value that the registration endpoint rejects.
raised.why_it_breaks: An install registered with `0.23.0` can later send an empty version string, or a 33-character version, through `/match`; the ledger persists that value in `ext_version`, even though the registration schema requires 1–32 characters.

raised.quote:
INSERT INTO install_usage_daily (date, install_id, shop, match_requests, match_beers, match_misses)
      VALUES (@date, @installId, @shop, @matchRequests, @matchBeers, @matchMisses)
      ON CONFLICT(date, install_id, shop) DO UPDATE SET
        match_requests = match_requests + excluded.match_requests,
        match_beers    = match_beers    + excluded.match_beers,
        match_misses   = match_misses   + excluded.match_misses
raised.claim: Per-install accounting has no row bound per day because the client controls the shop key.
raised.why_it_breaks: When an install reports a different accepted shop value on successive requests, every request creates a new row rather than incrementing an existing counter. The string-length limit and registration cap do not bound this storage growth per install.

raised.claim: The shared misses journal accepts indefinitely many distinct client-supplied misses from one install.
raised.why_it_breaks: Successive authenticated requests containing new normalized card identities that the matcher searches but cannot find each add durable journal rows. The registration cap does not limit writes from an existing token, and deleting the install intentionally leaves those rows behind.

raised.quote:
seen_days      = seen_days + (last_seen_date <> excluded.last_seen_date),
        last_seen_date = excluded.last_seen_date,
        last_seen_at   = excluded.last_seen_at,
        abv            = COALESCE(abv, excluded.abv)
raised.claim: The journal counts date transitions, not distinct dates, when sightings are persisted out of order.
raised.why_it_breaks: If a card's sightings are written in the order Monday, Tuesday, then a delayed Monday, `seen_days` becomes 3 instead of 2 and `last_seen_at` moves backward. The same date can then be counted again when another Tuesday sighting arrives.

raised.quote:
ON CONFLICT(normalized_brewery, normalized_name) DO UPDATE SET
        seen_days      = seen_days + (last_seen_date <> excluded.last_seen_date),
        last_seen_date = excluded.last_seen_date,
        last_seen_at   = excluded.last_seen_at,
        abv            = COALESCE(abv, excluded.abv)
raised.claim: The misses journal collapses cards with the same normalized text even when their ABVs identify different variants.
raised.why_it_breaks: If a shop has both a 0% and a 5% variant under the same brewery and name, misses for both update one row, retain whichever ABV was recorded first, and pool their sighting days. The stored row cannot show that both variants were missed.

raised.quote:
ON CONFLICT(normalized_brewery, normalized_name) DO UPDATE SET
        seen_days      = seen_days + (last_seen_date <> excluded.last_seen_date),
        last_seen_date = excluded.last_seen_date,
        last_seen_at   = excluded.last_seen_at,
        abv            = COALESCE(abv, excluded.abv)
raised.claim: A first sighting without shop metadata permanently leaves the journal row's shop blank.
raised.why_it_breaks: If an older client first reports a miss without `client.shop`, the journal stores an empty string. A later report of the same card from a known shop updates its date but cannot fill the missing shop, unlike the backfill for initially missing ABV.

raised.claim: The cap test uses the live clock for both its fixture and the later requests, so it can fail at Warsaw midnight.
raised.why_it_breaks: If `fillToCap` seeds the old date just before midnight and either request executes just after midnight, registration correctly uses the new day's allocation and returns 201 where the test expects 429.
